originality.rationale: The exact single-crossing comparison for every interior k-of-n quorum under a fixed marginal extinction rate, with a unique interior mean-time optimum in the smallest case, was not contained in the inspected primary sources or accessible same-slot historical claims. value.rationale: Ecological planning uses a quorum of simultaneously viable patches as a minimal connectivity/resilience proxy, not merely persistence of any one patch. The theorem gives a global, sharp time-horizon reversal uniform over every intermediate quorum and all symmetric hazard allocations with identical marginal extinction rates. The n=3,k=2 exact interior mean-time optimum is structurally informative because it is neither an all-independent nor an all-synchronized extreme, and it shows that integrating crossing survival curves can select a nontrivial mixture. The result does not claim broad ecological realism; its value is a complete benchmark for synchrony versus independent disturbance at fixed per-patch risk.
